title: Advice for a Healthy Student Lifestyle
writingModel: How to Stay Healthy at University: Advice for First-Year Students — by Rustam Seilov

Starting university is exciting. It is also physically and mentally demanding in ways that many students do not anticipate. If you are about to begin your first year, or if you are struggling with the health challenges of student life, this guide is for you.

First, you should take sleep seriously. You have to understand that sleep is not a luxury — it is a basic biological need. Research shows that students who sleep fewer than six hours a night perform significantly worse academically. You shouldn't stay up past 2 a.m. regularly, even during exam periods. Set a consistent bedtime and try to keep to it. You don't have to go to bed at 9 p.m. — but you should aim for seven hours minimum.

Second, you should eat regularly, even when you are busy. You don't have to cook elaborate meals. A piece of fruit, a bowl of porridge, a sandwich with protein — these are all better than nothing. You shouldn't skip breakfast. Your brain has to have fuel to function effectively. If you eat in the cafeteria, try to choose something that includes vegetables and protein, not just carbohydrates.

Third, you have to move your body regularly. At school, this was compulsory. At university, it is optional — which means you have to take personal responsibility for it. You don't have to train intensively. A thirty-minute walk three times a week is enough to produce measurable benefits. If you feel resistance to exercise, remember: you don't have to enjoy it. You just have to do it.

Fourth, you should protect your mental health. University should be challenging, but it shouldn't feel impossible. If you are feeling anxious, overwhelmed, or persistently low, you should talk to someone. WKU has a counselling service that is free and confidential. You don't have to be in crisis to use it. Going when things are manageable is smarter than waiting until they are not.

Finally, you should be kind to yourself. You don't have to be perfect. You don't have to have everything figured out. University is a process — the mistakes you make, the habits you build, and the adjustments you learn to make are all part of the education. Take care of your body and your mind. Everything else follows.
